scope: finite charged lifecycle decisions over architecture expansion, pruning, compilation, local/global morphogenesis, bounded deterministic generation recurrences, and deterministic finite developmental state spaces
assumptions: all lifecycle costs and losses are nonnegative integers and compared over a prospectively fixed finite horizon
expansion and pruning alternatives are obligation-equivalent except for explicitly charged residual loss
local morphogenesis may be selected only when the local patch is obligation-sufficient
the registered multi-generation recurrence holds parameters fixed over its bounded horizon
the finite-state impossibility result assumes deterministic closed dynamics on a fixed finite developmental state set
claim_boundary: This closes the final six bounded H rows with finite lifecycle/cycle laws. It does not establish empirical G7 developmental prediction, stochastic or expanding-state open-endedness, unbounded self-modification, natural evolution, or universal architecture policy.
strongest_parent: amortized replacement/expansion decisions, program compilation economics, local-vs-global optimization, dynamical-systems recurrence, pigeonhole principle on finite deterministic systems
negative_twin: a structural change that does not improve fully charged lifecycle cost, an obligation-insufficient local patch, or a finite deterministic system claimed to produce infinitely many distinct states
nearest_counterexample: stochastic dynamics, external novelty injection, or a developmental state space that can itself grow without bound falls outside the finite deterministic cycle theorem; changing future costs invalidates fixed-horizon lifecycle crossovers
falsifier: Any registered decision disagrees with direct fully charged totals, a local patch is selected while obligation-insufficient, the bounded generation recurrence is not reproduced exactly, or a deterministic closed finite-state trajectory visits more distinct states than the size of its registered state set before repeating.

rows.ledger_row: Predict when architecture expansion should occur.
rows.law: Over horizon H, keep cost is H*L_current. Expansion cost is X + H*(L_expanded + M_expanded). Expand iff the latter is strictly smaller; equality is a tie.
rows.negative_twin: expansion leaves loss unchanged while adding cost/maintenance; KEEP must win
rows.falsifier: EXPAND is selected when its fully charged horizon cost is not below KEEP

rows.ledger_row: Predict when old structure should be forgotten/pruned.
rows.law: Keep cost is H*(maintenance + retained-loss). Prune cost is P + H*post-prune-loss. Prune iff its fully charged cost is strictly smaller; load-bearing old structure may therefore be retained despite maintenance.
rows.negative_twin: pruning a load-bearing component creates enough residual loss that KEEP wins
rows.falsifier: PRUNE is selected when its fully charged cost is not below KEEP

rows.law: For reuse N, interpreted cost is N*i. Compiled cost is B + N*(c+v), including build B and verification v. Self-compilation wins iff B + N*(c+v) < N*i.
rows.negative_twin: verification exactly erases compiled per-use saving, producing no eventual strict advantage when build cost is zero
rows.falsifier: COMPILE is selected when its charged total is not below interpretation

rows.law: A local developmental patch may compete with global rebuild only if obligation-sufficient. Conditional on sufficiency, local total P+V+H*L_residual is chosen iff below global rebuild cost G.
rows.negative_twin: a cheap local patch that is obligation-insufficient must still lose to global rebuild
rows.falsifier: LOCAL is selected despite failed obligation sufficiency or without a charged cost advantage

rows.law: Registered bounded burden trajectory obeys b[g+1]=max(0,b[g]-s)+m for fixed inherited reduction s and maintenance m; exact generation-by-generation receipts distinguish convergence, fixed points and growth.
rows.negative_twin: maintenance larger than inherited reduction drives burden upward rather than guaranteeing cumulative improvement
rows.falsifier: recorded trajectory differs from the frozen recurrence at any generation

rows.law: For deterministic closed transition F on finite state set X, any trajectory repeats a state after at most |X| distinct visits. From the first repeat onward it is eventually periodic, so infinitely many distinct developmental states/morphologies are impossible without state-space growth, stochastic/external novelty, or another premise change.
rows.strongest_parent: pigeonhole principle / finite deterministic dynamical systems
rows.negative_twin: a system whose registered state space can grow is outside the fixed-finite theorem rather than a counterexample
rows.falsifier: a closed deterministic transition on finite X produces more than |X| distinct states before the first repeat
